_doc: Batch m11 (medium, opus themed pass): tanuki, coati band, macaque troop, capuchin pickpocket, wildcat, caracal, fishing cat, jaguarundi, jaguar cub pair, bear cub tumble, sun bear. Motifs in motifs/medium_m11.js; every creature has its own signature motif with its own chain effect. Shared inside the batch: cat-claw (wildcat, caracal; own palettes), honey-paw (bear cub, sun bear). Reused from the catalogue: mud-flop (jaguar cubs Mud Roll), bee-pollen (bear cub Bee-Chase Bowl).

tanuki.notes: A round masked tanuki from folk tales: a leaf on its head lets it shape-shift into a leaf, a stump or a kettle, and it drums on its round belly. The thing to draw is the dark mask and the leaf.

p.u0: Belly Drum: round pale bellies drum at spots along the edge, a beat ring popping out on every beat, tied in a tripping rhythm line

u1.n: Leaf Disguise: the tanuki puts its leaf on and vanishes in a white poof, then peeks back out of the smoke

u2.n: Rolling Barge: the tanuki curls into a furry ball, rolls out of the edge with its mask band turning and drops back

u3.n: Stump Pose: the tanuki turns into a ring-cut stump with a leaf on top along the edge, its striped tail peeking out, eyes blinking in the bark

p.b0: Whiskered Paw: masked faces launch off the edge, whiskers bristling and a paw swiping

b1.n: Belly Drum Slam: drumming bellies launch off the edge one after another, beat rings popping

b2.n: Stump Stance: leaf-topped stumps plant along the edge, dust settling round the roots

b3.n: Disguised Charge: a harmless leaf shoves out of the edge, poofs, and the tanuki inside barges and drops back

coati-band.notes: A band of rainforest coatis walking in a line with their long ringed tails held straight up like flags, rooting under logs and leaf litter with long, upturned snouts.

u0.n: Ringtail Screen: ringed tails cross into a picket screen that pushes out of the edge, the dark and pale bands pulsing

u1.n: Log Cover: a mossy fallen log lines the edge, coati snouts poking out from under it in turn

u2.n: Snout Poke: long upturned snouts poke at spots round the edge, tips twitching, tied in a tripping line

p.u3: Tail Flag: ringed tails shoot up out of the edge like flags, tips curling, leaves falling past

b0.n: Log-Turning Rake: snouts dig out of the edge one after another, rotten-log crumbs thrown

b1.n: Striped-Flag Pile-On: a thicket of ringed tails piles out of the edge and drops back

b2.n: Tail-Flag Huddle: ringed tails huddle in a screen along the edge, bands breathing

b3.n: Under-Log Barge: the log heaves out of the edge with coatis barging under it and drops back

macaque-troop.notes: A troop of grey-brown mountain macaques with bare pink faces and short tails: snow monkeys that soak in steaming hot springs, stuff their cheek pouches and flash an open-mouth threat.

p.u0: Troop Shove: pink faces shove out of the edge with an open-mouth threat and drop back

u1.n: Cheek Dump: cheeks bulge with food, the faces push out and dump seeds and fruit scraps on the foe

u2.n: Troop Huddle: macaques huddle in a steaming hot spring along the edge, snow on their crowns, steam curling up

u3.n: Quick Fingers: pink-palmed hands launch off the edge, fingers spread, and snatch shut

b0.n: Quick-Finger Grab: grabbing hands fly off the edge, food crumbs dropping from them

b1.n: Troop Pile-On: the whole steaming huddle piles off the edge one head after another

b2.n: Mountain Hunch: hunched pink faces hold the edge in falling snow, brows raised

b3.n: Elder's Shove: one big old face shoves out of the edge with a wide threat and drops back

capuchin-pickpocket.notes: A small, clever rainforest capuchin with a cream face and shoulders under a dark cap: it picks pockets, steals shiny buttons and pelts you with fruit from the canopy.

u0.n: Pocket Snag: a little hand dips pocket to pocket along the whole edge and comes out with a glinting coin

u1.n: Fruit Bomb: round orange fruit are lobbed out of the edge and splat with juice

u2.n: Canopy Perch: the capuchin swings out on a leafy branch, hanging by its curled tail, and swings back

u3.n: Button Snatch: shiny four-hole buttons hang at spots on their threads, glinting, tied in a tripping line

b0.n: Light-Finger Grab: hands dip out of the edge one after another, each lifting a coin

b1.n: Button Swipe: snatched buttons fly off the edge on their threads, glinting

p.b2: Cream-Face Shrug: cream faces under dark caps hold the edge, shrugging with a cheeky grin

b3.n: Bump-and-Lift: a grinning face bumps out of the edge and is gone again

wildcat.notes: A grey striped wildcat of forest edge and grassland, like a big tabby: the thing to draw is the thick blunt tail with dark rings and a black tip; it bristles, flattens its ears and hisses.

u0.n: Fur Bristle: arched tabby backs push out of the edge with the fur standing up in spikes

u1.n: Claw Swipe: tabby paws launch off the edge with claws sprung, three curved slash marks behind

u2.n: Ear Flat Guard: amber-eyed faces flatten their ears and hiss, springing out and back

p.u3: Tail Ring Feint: thick ringed tails lash out of the edge and whip back, drawing the eye

b0.n: Striped Slash: claw paws streak off the edge, angry marks popping

b1.n: Thick-Tail Mangle: the heavy ringed tail slams out of the edge and drops back, the wildcat behind it

b2.n: Wary Crouch: faces hold the edge with ears half back, watching

b3.n: Tomcat Shove: a bristling arched back shoves out of the edge and drops back

caracal.notes: A plain tawny caracal of desert scrub with very long black ear tufts that it flicks to signal; it leaps straight up to swat birds out of the air and rests in the grass at dusk.

u0.n: Bird Leap: small birds flush off the edge and a tawny paw leaps up after each, feathers bursting

u1.n: Dusk Rest: a caracal lies low in the grass before an orange half sun, ear tufts twitching, and rises

u2.n: Scrub Cover: dry thorny scrub springs up round the edge, two black ear tufts poking above it, and sinks back

p.u3: Tuft Flick: the long black ear tufts flick out of the edge one way and the other and pull back

b0.n: Pen-Tuft Rake: tawny paws rake off the edge, claws out, desert dust behind

b1.n: Bird-Snatch Leap: a caracal springs straight out of the edge, snatches a bird and drops back

p.b2: Tufted Crouch: tufted heads hold the edge, the tufts twitching

b3.n: Sly Bush-Slink: a scrub bush slinks out of the edge, ear tufts showing, and drops back

fishing-cat.notes: A stocky, spotted, olive-grey fishing cat of wetland and mangrove: it wades and dives, its webbed paws scooping fish out of the water, and its dense coat sheds the wet.

u0.n: Wet Plate: stocky spotted backs line the edge half under water, drops beading and running off

u1.n: Fur Shake: fur shakes out of the edge flinging a ring of drops and pulls back

u2.n: Paw Flick: one webbed paw flicks its way along the whole edge, drops flying

p.u3: Scoop Grab: webbed paws scoop silver fish out of the water at spots, tied in a tripping line

b0.n: Scooping Paw: webbed paws launch off the edge one after another, claws hooked

b1.n: Wading Pounce: the cat pounces out of the shallows with a splash and drops back

b2.n: Stocky Wade Stance: wet spotted backs hold the edge, bubbles rising

b3.n: Spotted Shoulder Shove: a wet spotted shoulder shoves out of the edge and drops back

jaguarundi.notes: A long, low, plain-coated jaguarundi with a small round head and a long tail: the otter-cat of riverbanks and tall grass, slipping past unseen and chirping to its kind.

u0.n: River Slip: slick wet streaks hang at spots, a dark back slipping into the water at each, splash rings tied in a tripping line

u1.n: Otter Cat Pounce: a long low body pounces out of the edge like an otter and drops back

u2.n: Bank Cover: tall bank grass parts round the edge and the plain dark back slips away between

u3.n: Unseen Cross: a dark silhouette blinks from spot to spot, only two eyes glinting

p.b0: Otter-Long Swipe: long low bodies streak off the edge one after another

b1.n: Hidden Crossing Pounce: dark silhouettes strike off the edge, eyes glinting as they come

b2.n: Plain-Coat Crouch: long low bodies flatten along the edge, all but invisible

b3.n: Reappearing Barge: the grass bursts open as the cat barges out of the edge and closes as it drops back

jaguar-cub-pair.notes: Two small spotted jaguar cubs with oversized paws and stubby tails: they play-wrestle, chase their own tails, roll in mud and steal bootlaces.

u0.n: Cub Spring: oversized spotted paws spring off the edge, toes spreading as they bat

u1.n: Tail Chase: a cub spins in a circle after its own stubby tail, popping up at one spot after another

u2.n: Mud Roll: the cubs roll out of the edge in a spray of mud splats and come back muddy

u3.n: Lace Grab: bootlace bows hang at spots and a paw tugs each loose, the laces tying the foe up

p.b0: Spotted Pounce: wrestling cub pairs tumble off the edge one after another

b1.n: Twin Cub Tackle: both cubs tackle out of the edge together and tumble back

b2.n: Rosette Stance: big spotted paws plant along the edge, toes flexing

b3.n: Bootlace Swat: a paw swats a bootlace out of the edge and it flops back

bear-cub-tumble.notes: Round, fluffy brown bear cubs of forest and mountain that curl into balls and roll downhill, raid hives for honey and get chased by the bees.

p.u0: Cub Roll: fluffy cubs curl up tight in balls along the edge, rocking

u1.n: Honey Raid: a sticky paw slams out of a honeycomb, honey dripping, and drops back

u2.n: Tumble Cover: ferns spring up round the edge and part, a round cub head peeking out, then sink back

u3.n: Hillside Bowl: curled cub balls bowl off the edge one after another, rolling

b0.n: Cub Paw Swipe: sticky paws swipe off the edge, honey flying

b1.n: Bee-Chase Bowl: angry striped bees loop off the edge after the cub, pollen trailing

b2.n: Roll-Up Hunker: the cubs roll up in balls along the edge, a puff where each settles

b3.n: Downhill Shoulder Roll: a cub ball rolls out of the edge and bumps back

sun-bear.notes: A small, black rainforest sun bear with a pale gold muzzle and a gold crescent on its chest like a rising sun: it climbs, rips bark with long claws and licks honey with a very long tongue.

u0.n: Sun Claw: one paw of long pale sickle claws rips its way along the whole edge, bark strips peeling

u1.n: Honey Rest: a honey-dripping paw rises from the comb as the bear licks it clean

u2.n: Bark Hide: the bear presses itself to a trunk, arms wrapped round, springs out and back peeking one side then the other

u3.n: Sniff Out: pale gold muzzles push out of the edge snuffling, scent lines curling, termites scattering

b0.n: Honey-Paw Swipe: sticky paws swipe off the edge, honey dripping

b1.n: Crescent Bear-Hug: the gold crescent glows as the bear lunges out of the edge for a hug and drops back

p.b2: Gold-Crescent Stance: black bears hold the edge, their gold chest crescents glowing like rising suns

b3.n: Long-Tongue Raid: a muzzle shoves out to a bark hole and the long pink tongue raids it for honey
